channel.title: Theatre Updates
channel.description: Signed updates for Theatre for macOS.

item.description:
# Theatre 0.2.0
Multiple Jellyfin servers in one library, smoother artwork loading, and more reliable browsing and playback. This release includes the full update since 0.1.1.
## Multiple servers
- Connect your first server through the existing onboarding, then add more from **Theatre → Server → Add Server…**. - Browse Home, Continue, Recently Added, Movies, Shows, search, and downloads across connected servers. Movies and Shows include a server filter. - Each server has its own address, username, saved session, and Sign Out action. Signing out of every server returns to onboarding. Passwords are never displayed or saved. - **Theatre → Refresh Library** offers individual servers and **Refresh All**. **⌘R** refreshes every connected server. - Playback, artwork, details, watch history, and offline progress use the title’s own server and account. Existing download catalogs and files are retained; signing out hides that account’s downloads rather than deleting them.
## Loading and browsing
- Covers use Jellyfin’s BlurHash metadata for an immediate 64-pixel blurred preview, then fade to the loaded artwork without an extra preview request. Cached artwork appears immediately, and Reduce Motion disables the transition. - Neutral placeholders reserve space while recommendations, posters, details, seasons, episodes, and cast pages load. - Session caches reuse library pages, details, seasons, filter options, person pages, searches, and artwork. Refresh and watch-progress changes invalidate browsing data; Continue and Recently Added remain live. - Library and search pages load more results automatically as you scroll. Fixed stale search responses and pagination using a previous query’s offset. - Fixed multi-server search pagination when Jellyfin returns results by relevance rather than alphabetical order. - Fixed Recently Added being filled with virtual episode records instead of available movies and shows, and a query flag that could cause Jellyfin 10.11 to ignore search filtering. - Improved season, episode, and person-page loading so refreshes preserve existing content while new data arrives.
## HTTPS compatibility
HTTPS direct playback now uses URLSession for ranged network reads while VLC decodes the original video, improving compatibility with modern TLS servers. API requests, artwork, downloads, and HTTPS direct playback also accept unverified certificates, including self-signed certificates.
**These Jellyfin HTTPS connections are encrypted, but Theatre does not verify the server’s identity.** Only connect to servers you trust. Authenticated redirects remain restricted to the original server. See [privacy information](https://github.com/clement-horesh/theatre/blob/v0.2.0/PRIVACY.md).
## Installation and updates
Download **Theatre-0.2.0.dmg**, open it, and drag Theatre into Applications. Theatre requires your own Jellyfin server and account; no media or server is bundled.
Existing 0.1.1 users can use **Theatre → Update App → Check for Updates…**. The original 0.1.0 beta needs one manual installation to acquire the updater. The update archive and feed are signed with the existing Sparkle key.
This release is for **Apple Silicon Macs**, targets macOS 13 or later, and is **ad-hoc signed, not notarized by Apple**. If macOS blocks the first launch, follow the documented **System Settings → Privacy & Security → Open Anyway** process. Ad-hoc updates may ask for Keychain authorization again. See [installation instructions](https://github.com/clement-horesh/theatre/blob/v0.2.0/INSTALL.md).
## Known limitations
- Search retains Jellyfin’s native matching: `spider` or `Spider-Man` matches the title; `spiderman` without the hyphen does not. - Intel and older macOS versions have not been verified. HDR/Dolby Vision accuracy, surround output, and AirPlay still need hardware validation. PiP and AirPlay format support depends on AVPlayer and Jellyfin transcoding permissions. - Signing out does not delete downloaded media. Use download removal controls to delete saved files.
## License and source
Theatre is licensed under **GPL-3.0-only**. VLCKit and its components retain their upstream licenses; notices are included in the app. GitHub provides source archives for this release tag. Corresponding VLC and dependency sources remain available in the separate [Third-party sources release](https://github.com/clement-horesh/theatre/releases/tag/third-party-vlckit-3.7.2). Only the DMG is needed for manual installation.

# Theatre 0.1.1
A native Mac client for your Jellyfin server. This release is for Apple Silicon Macs and is ad-hoc signed, not Apple-notarized.
## Changes in 0.1.1
- In-app updates through Sparkle: the macOS **Theatre → Update App** menu checks daily, indicates a newer version with a dot, and offers a native install/restart flow. Automatic checks can be disabled. Scheduled checks do not interrupt playback; update feeds and archives are signed and verified. - Download preparation and transfers share a limit of two concurrent jobs. Catalog and file operations run off the main thread, progress no longer refreshes the whole library, and queued transfers have Pause/Resume/Retry controls. - Compatible-stream retries retain the current playback position and paused state. Playback cleanup handles cancellation during native preparation. - Fixed credits markers being omitted from requests, which prevented early **Next Episode** prompts. Skip Intro and Next Episode now sit to the left of the bottom-right player controls. - Authenticated requests reject redirects to another origin or scheme. Failure logs avoid exposing stream URLs and credentials. - Library loading, recommendations, trailer selection, and episode keyboard actions have reliability and consistency improvements. - Reorganized the native Theatre menu, grouping connection information and Sign Out under Server. Information uses the same grouped form style as Settings.
## Included
- Jellyfin sign-in with the server-issued session token saved in Keychain. - Home recommendations, Continue, Recently Added, search, and Movies/Shows libraries with grid and alphabetical views and filters. - Movie and show details, seasons, episodes, cast and crew, actor filmographies, related titles, and Jellyfin-provided remote trailers. - Broad-format VLC playback, resume, audio and subtitle selection, subtitle styling, keyboard/media controls, and automatic next-episode playback. - Skip Intro and credits actions when Jellyfin provides valid markers. - Offline downloads with pause/resume/retry, cached artwork, and watch-progress synchronization. - Dark appearance, native Mac controls, Liquid Glass on supported macOS versions, and hover/focus feedback.
## Installation
Download **Theatre-0.1.1.dmg**, drag Theatre into Applications, and connect to your own Jellyfin server. No media or server is bundled. Existing 0.1.0 users need this manual installation once to acquire the updater; subsequent updates can be installed from **Theatre → Update App**.
This build is not notarized. If macOS blocks it as an unidentified developer, use Apple’s **System Settings → Privacy & Security → Open Anyway** process after attempting to open the app. Read [installation instructions](INSTALL.md) for details and limitations.
The build targets macOS 13 or later; hands-on validation has been on macOS 27.2. Intel and older macOS validation remain outstanding. HDR/Dolby Vision accuracy, surround output, and AirPlay require further hardware checks. PiP and AirPlay format support depends on AVPlayer and Jellyfin transcoding permissions. Ad-hoc updates may prompt again for Jellyfin session access in Keychain; update signature verification itself does not require Keychain access.
## License and source
Theatre is licensed under **GPL-3.0-only**. VLCKit and its components retain their upstream licenses; notices are included in the app. GitHub provides Theatre’s source archives automatically. VLC and dependency sources are available in the separate [Third-party sources release](https://github.com/clement-horesh/theatre/releases/tag/third-party-vlckit-3.7.2). Only the DMG is needed to install the app. See [third-party notices](Vendor/THIRD-PARTY-NOTICES.md).
